text.en:
Sheela chewed a piece of chapati for a long time and noticed it tasted slightly sweet.
"Your saliva has started to change the starch into sugar," said her teacher. "Your food now begins a long journey through your body."

Animals take in food (ingestion), break it down into simple substances (digestion), absorb the simple substances into the blood (absorption), use them for energy and growth (assimilation), and remove undigested waste (egestion).
In humans, food enters the mouth where teeth chew it and saliva starts digesting starch. It goes down the food pipe (oesophagus) to the stomach, where acid and juices digest it further. In the small intestine digestion ends and digested food is absorbed into the blood. The large intestine absorbs water and the rest leaves as waste.
The liver makes bile that helps digest fats. The pancreas makes juices that digest food. Chewing well, eating on time and washing hands keep the digestive system healthy.
Nutrition has steps: taking in food, digestion, absorption, using the food and removing waste.
Food is chewed in the mouth. Saliva begins to digest starch.
In the stomach, acid and juices digest food. In the small intestine digestion ends and food is absorbed.
The large intestine absorbs water. The rest leaves as waste.

problem.en: Where does most absorption of digested food take place?

text.en: Digestion is completed in the small intestine.

why.en: Food is in tiny simple forms.

text.en: The small intestine is long and has a large surface.
So most digested food is absorbed in the small intestine.

prompt.en: A friend says food is digested only in the stomach. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: Digestion starts in the mouth and finishes in the small intestine.
The stomach is only one step.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the stomach does all digestion.

points.en: Nutrition: ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation, egestion.
Digestion starts in the mouth and ends in the small intestine.
